newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse sees radio revenues rise. [CORRECTED 19:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse sees radio revenues rise. [CORRECTED 19:15 GMT]

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp said that for the first full year of operations after its acquisition of CBS radio stations operating cash flows in the radio group are projected to increase about 50 percent on 12 percent higher revenues.
(Corrects to say the projection is only for CBS radio stations).
Westinghouse won approval today from the Federal Communications Commission to merge with Infinity Broadcasting Corp. Westinghouse is to acquire Infinity's 43 radio stations as part of the merger.
Westinghouse also got permanent one-to-a-market waivers from the commission to keep the stations that it had acquired from CBS Inc in November 1995.
It said the new radio group would have combined revenues totaling more than $1 billion with 79 radio stations in 17 markets.
Westinghouse said the commission's approvals were the final steps needed before going ahead with the merger.
